text:
emily: Heads up — Acme reported 403 when they try to switch to their billing org from the console after completing the device/OIDC device_code flow. Token looks valid on their side. Repro steps below, customer says this started after we rolled the new short-lived device tokens.

emily: Repro steps (from customer):
```
1) Visit https://console.redwood.ai/auth/device
2) Complete device code on device auth page
3) Console shows logged in but when they click Settings > Billing > Switch org -> 403
4) curl to /api/v1/orgs/billing/switch with Authorization: Bearer <token> returns 403
```

devon: can you paste the actual curl response body (redact token)? also need the session id from the console devtools. @jordan FYI might be auth-scope related. :thinking_face:

emily: customer paste (redacted):
```
$ curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJ***REDACTED***abc" https://api.redwood.ai/api/v1/orgs/billing/switch 
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
{
  "error": "forbidden",
  "message": "missing required role: billing.admin (or insufficient org scope)"
}
```

jordan: thanks. quick theory: device_code/OIDC device flow tokens are being minted without the optional `roles` or `org:read` scopes by default. Our gateway mapping expects a roles claim on access_token for org switch checks. If the token is short-lived and only meant for console session, we sometimes rely on id_token for claims — but device flow might not return id_token at all depending on provider config.

luis: looking at gateway logs for that session_id, I see: `auth.method=device_code`, `scopes=openid profile`, no `roles` or `org:read` scope. Gateway did not call the introspection endpoint because token type flagged as "local" per new device token policy. We have a fail path that denies org-level actions if roles claim missing.

jordan: OK. two paths: (1) short-term workaround for customer: ask them to re-auth via regular OAuth auth_code flow (this will include id_token + groups/roles) or request token with `org:read billing.admin` scope if their IdP supports it. (2) longer-term: we should fallback to introspecting token or fetching userinfo if access_token lacks roles and auth.method=device_code. I'll open an eng ticket.

emily: confirmed customer tried auth_code flow and switching works. They're blocked until they can use a browser-based login; device flow isn't working for their CI-like device case. Customer accepted workaround for now but needs device flow fixed.

jordan: creating ENG ticket: ENG-5389 "map roles for device_code tokens by introspection or id_token fallback". Proposed patch: if auth.method == device_code and access_token lacks roles, call introspection + userinfo before rejecting. Also add telemetry to avoid extra introspections for tokens we trust.

luis: infra note: we intentionally minimized introspection on device tokens to reduce load when we rolled the short-lived tokens. We'll add a conditional call only for org-change endpoints to limit cost.

devon: created support ticket to track customer escalation SUP-2190 and logged the workaround. Leaving a note for docs team to add a compatibility bullet under "Device flow limitations".

emily: Customer happy for now, thanks team. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident logged: INC-2026 (low) linked to ENG-5389 and SUP-2190 — automated alert created for any additional 403 spikes on /api/v1/orgs/* endpoints for device_code auth.
